get.description: Get kws setting values for the user

parameters.description: DOB of the user in YYYY-MM-DD
parameters.name: dob

parameters.description: Location of the user, example US-CA
parameters.name: location

parameters.description: Whether parental controls should be enforced, might trigger an email to parent to review limits
parameters.name: enforce_parental_control

parameters.description: The relative time zone of the user based off IANA Time Zone database
parameters.name: time_zone

parameters.description: full to include settings definitions in the response. (Default: short)
parameters.name: format

dob.description: DOB of the user in YYYY-MM-DD

enforce_parental_control.description: Whether parental controls should be enforced (might trigger an email to the parent to review limits)

location.description: Location of the user, example US-CA

timezone.description: The relative time zone of the user based off IANA Time Zone database

content_type.description: The HTTP Content-Type header value specifying the content type of the body.

data.description: The HTTP request/response body as raw binary.

extensions.description:
Application specific response metadata. Must be set in the first response
for streaming APIs.

allow_product_overrides.description: Determines whether or not settings can be overridden and specifies if overrides are limited to values, translations, regions or age brackets

data_storage.description: Whether the setting data should be stored

increment_or_decrement_by.description: The value to apply for each increment or decrement. i.e. a value of 2 would result in 6 incrementing to 8 or decrementing to 4

inherit_from_org.description: Whether the setting was inherited from the organisation level

max.description: The maximum value for a numeric setting

maximum_schedule_windows_per_day.description: The maximum number of schedule windows allowed for the particular setting

min.description: The minimum value for a numeric setting

number_of_decimals.description: The number of decimals for a numeric setting

numeric_value_format.description: The numeric value type (decimal, integer, etc)

org_id.description: The organisation ID of the setting

product_id.description: The product ID of a product-level setting

restrictive_order.description: The type of restrictiveOrder that corresponds with the value type of the setting. The restrictiveOrder can be oneOf 'firstRestrictive', 'firstPermissive' for valueType 'option' 'lowRestrictive', 'lowPermissive' for valueType 'numeric' 'falseRestrictive', 'falsePermissive' for valueType 'boolean' 'earlierRestrictive', 'earlierPermissive' for valueType 'date'

schedule_period.description: The configured schedule periods, can be 5m, 10m, 15m, 30m 1h, 1d

setting_name.description: The name used to identify the setting

user_hidden.description: Whether the setting is visible to a child user or not

value_type.description: The type of setting value (boolean, numeric, option, etc)

value.description: The value for the setting option

apply_consent_to_enforced_users_only.description: The consent required from the parent for the age bracket

consent_type.description: The type of consent required for the age bracket

effective_source.description: How the effective value was determined (one of default, preference, parentLimit, enforcedLimit).

is_org_level.description: True if the full setting is from an org-level setting and false if it is from a product-level setting (only relevant when using setting inheritance)

last_graduated_at.description: The unix timestamp in milliseconds for the date/time that the user last graduated to a different age-bracket.

parent_limit_from_org_level.description: True if the parent limit value is from an org-level setting and false if it is from a product-level setting (only relevant when using setting inheritance)

parent_limit_schedule.description: A hashmap containing the parent limit schedule, with keys as time window and value as the parent limit

parent_limit_schedule_enabled.description: True if the parent limit schedule is enabled, indicating that a schedule may have been used in calculation of users effective value.

parent_limit_updated_at.description: The unix timestamp in milliseconds for the date/time that the parent limit was last updated. If null, it indicates that the user is using the default

preferred_value_from_org_level.description: True if the preferred value is from an org-level setting and false if it is from a product-level setting (only relevant when using setting inheritance)

preferred_value_updated_at.description: The unix timestamp in milliseconds for the date/time that the preferred value was last updated. If null, it indicates that the user is using the default

schedule_calculated_from_time_zone.description: Time Zone used in the calculation of a users effective value when a parentLimitSchedule is enabled

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com. As of May 2023, there are no widely used type server
implementations and no plans to implement one.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

protobufNullValue.description:
`NullValue` is a singleton enumeration to represent the null value for the
`Value` type union.

The JSON representation for `NullValue` is JSON `null`.

 - NULL_VALUE: Null value.
